subject: All Subjects
summary: a mixed set modelled on the most-repeated GATE ME previous-year concepts across all subjects: analogies and clock angles, Laplace shifting and Simpson's rule, the ballistic pendulum, thin-cylinder volumetric strain, Hooke's joint, transmissibility, belt power, jet impact on a moving plate, Prandtl number, entropy of the universe, the optimum Brayton pressure ratio, top-gate filling time and Little's law

questions.text: Select the pair that has the same relationship as AUTHOR : NOVEL
solution: Concept: In analogy questions, state the relation in one sentence and test each option with the same sentence.
'An author creates a novel.' Only 'a sculptor creates a statue' fits the same sentence.
A reader uses a library, a teacher works in a classroom, and a pen writes on paper: none is creator → creation.
Answer: (B)
Exam tip: If two options seem to fit, make the relation sentence more specific (creator–creation, part–whole, worker–tool).

questions.text: The angle (in degrees) between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 3:40 is ______
solution: Concept: The minute hand moves 6° per minute and the hour hand 0.5° per minute, so θ = |30H − 5.5M|.
Check: minute hand at 240°, hour hand at 90 + 20 = 110°, difference 130° (clock face below).
Exam tip: If the formula gives more than 180°, subtract it from 360° to get the smaller angle.

questions.text: The Laplace transform of f(t) = t e<sup>−2t</sup> is
solution: Concept: First shifting theorem: L{eat f(t)} = F(s − a).
L{t} = 1/s²; with a = −2 the shift gives F(s + 2) = 1/(s + 2)².
Answer: (A)
Exam tip: L{tⁿ eat} = n!/(s − a)n+1; watch the sign of a when shifting.

questions.text: The integral of x⁴ from x = 0 to x = 2 is evaluated by Simpson's 1/3 rule with a step size of 0.5. The value obtained (round off to three decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: Simpson's 1/3 rule: I ≈ (h/3)[y0 + 4(y1 + y3) + 2y2 + y4], with an even number of strips.
The exact value is 32/5 = 6.4; the error comes from the fourth derivative (24), which is not zero.
Exam tip: Simpson's 1/3 rule is exact for polynomials up to degree 3, not degree 4.

questions.text: A bullet of mass 20 g moving horizontally at 400 m/s embeds itself in a 4 kg wooden block hanging from light strings (ballistic pendulum), as shown. Taking g = 9.81 m/s², the height (in mm) through which the block rises (round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: The impact is perfectly plastic: momentum is conserved during impact (energy is not); after impact, energy is conserved during the swing.
Common velocity V = mv/(m + M) = 0.02 × 400/4.02 = 1.990 m/s
Exam tip: Never equate the bullet's kinetic energy to (m + M)gh: more than 99 % of it is lost in the plastic impact.

questions.text: A thin cylindrical shell of diameter d and wall thickness t (closed ends) is subjected to an internal pressure p. With E the Young's modulus and ν the Poisson's ratio, its volumetric strain is
solution: Concept: σh = pd/(2t), σl = pd/(4t); volumetric strain = 2εh + εl.
ε<sub>h</sub> = (pd/(4tE))(2 − ν), ε<sub>l</sub> = (pd/(4tE))(1 − 2ν)
Exam tip: For a thin sphere, εv = 3ε = (3pd/(4tE))(1 − ν).

questions.text: The driving shaft of a Hooke's (universal) joint runs at a uniform 600 rpm, and the angle between the two shafts is 20°. The maximum and minimum speeds of the driven shaft are
solution: Concept: For a Hooke's joint, ωmax = ω/cos α and ωmin = ω cos α.
Nmin = 600 × 0.9397 = 563.8 rpm. Answer (D)
Exam tip: The maximum speed occurs twice per revolution; a double Hooke's joint (equal angles, forks in one plane) removes the fluctuation.

questions.text: For a spring-mass-damper system excited by a harmonic force, the transmissibility equals 1 at a frequency ratio ω/ωₙ of
opts: √2 only when the system is undamped
solution: Concept: TR = √[(1 + (2ζr)²)/((1 − r²)² + (2ζr)²)].
TR = 1 requires (1 − r²)² = 1, i.e. r² = 2, r = √2, independent of ζ: all the TR curves cross at r = √2.
Answer: (B)
Exam tip: Isolation (TR < 1) needs r > √2, and there more damping slightly increases TR.

questions.text: An open flat-belt drive has an angle of contact of 165° on the smaller pulley and a coefficient of friction of 0.3. The belt speed is 15 m/s and the tension on the tight side is 2000 N (centrifugal tension neglected). The power transmitted (in kW, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: T1/T2 = eμθ with θ in radians; P = (T1 − T2)v.
Exam tip: Use the angle of contact on the smaller pulley, where slip occurs first.

questions.text: A water jet of 40 mm diameter with a velocity of 25 m/s strikes normally a flat plate that moves away from the nozzle in the direction of the jet at 10 m/s, as shown. The force exerted by the jet on the plate (in N, round off to one decimal place) is ______
solution: Concept: For a single moving plate, the mass striking per second is ρA(V − u) and the relative velocity destroyed is (V − u), so F = ρA(V − u)².
The work done on the plate is F × u = 2827 W.
Exam tip: For a series of plates (a wheel), the whole jet ρAV strikes, so F = ρAV(V − u) instead.

questions.text: For laminar flow over a flat plate, the hydrodynamic boundary layer and the thermal boundary layer have the same thickness when
opts: the Biot number is less than 0.1
solution: Concept: δt/δ ≈ Pr−1/3, because Pr = ν/α compares momentum diffusion with heat diffusion.
When Pr = 1, momentum and heat diffuse at the same rate, so δ<sub>t</sub> = δ.
Answer: (A)
Exam tip: Liquid metals (Pr ≪ 1) have δt ≫ δ; oils (Pr ≫ 1) have δt ≪ δ.

questions.text: 1 kg of water (c = 4.18 kJ/kg·K) at 20 °C is placed in contact with a large reservoir at 80 °C until it reaches 80 °C. The entropy change of the universe (in kJ/K, round off to three decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: ΔSuniverse = ΔSwater + ΔSreservoir; the reservoir stays at constant temperature.
ΔS<sub>water</sub> = mc ln(T<sub>2</sub>/T<sub>1</sub>) = 4.18 ln(353.15/293.15) = 0.7784 kJ/K
ΔS<sub>reservoir</sub> = −Q/T = −4.18 × 60/353.15 = −0.7102 kJ/K
ΔSuniverse = 0.068 kJ/K (positive, as heat flows through a finite temperature difference)
Exam tip: Always use kelvin in ln(T2/T1) and in Q/T.

questions.text: An ideal Brayton cycle with air (γ = 1.4) works between a minimum temperature of 300 K and a maximum temperature of 1200 K. The pressure ratio that gives the maximum net work per kg of air is about
solution: Concept: Net work is maximum when T2 = T4 = √(TminTmax), giving rp = (Tmax/Tmin)γ/(2(γ − 1)).
At this ratio, T<sub>2</sub> = T<sub>4</sub> = 600 K.
Exam tip: At the pressure ratio (Tmax/Tmin)γ/(γ − 1) (= 128 here) the net work falls to zero.

questions.text: A mould cavity of volume 1.0 × 10⁶ mm³ is filled through a top gate, as shown. The height of molten metal above the gate (sprue height) is 200 mm and the gate area is 400 mm². Neglecting friction and taking g = 9.81 m/s², the filling time (in s, round off to two decimal places) is ______
solution: Concept: In a top gate the head stays constant during filling (metal falls freely into the cavity), so v = √(2gh) throughout and t = V/(A v).
Exam tip: For a bottom gate the effective head falls as the cavity fills, and t = (Am/Ag)(2/√(2g))(√ht − √(ht − hm)), which is longer.

questions.text: A machine shop holds on average 30 jobs as work-in-process, and it completes 6 jobs per day in steady state. The average time a job spends in the shop is
solution: Concept: Little's law: L = λW, valid for any stable system regardless of distributions.
W = L/λ = 30/6 = 5 days, answer (D)
Exam tip: Little's law also gives Lq = λWq; it is the quickest check on any queuing answer.
